evidence.reason: `runGitIn` is meant to route any input-carrying git call through `pipedGit`, as the comment at lines 109-110 states ("input-carrying calls (hash-object, diff-tree, cat-file --batch) run through the piped form"). The guard at line 108 adds `&& options.input.length > 0`, so a caller passing an empty `Uint8Array` (e.g. `git hash-object --stdin` for an empty blob, or `cat-file --batch`/`diff-tree --stdin` with zero inputs) falls into the `execFile` branch. `execFile` spawns the child with a stdin pipe that the parent never writes to or ends, so a git subcommand that reads stdin to EOF blocks until `EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` kills it instead of returning the correct result. `pipedGit` already terminates the pipe via `child.stdin.end(input)`, which correctly signals EOF for a zero-length input, so the smallest compatible fix is to test only `options?.input !== undefined`. This is an ordinary implementation defect in existing intended behavior, not a scope or requirement change.
